overview: This bill, called the Balance the Scales Act, changes how the Labor Department can help lawyers who sue employers over retirement and other workplace benefit plans covered by ERISA, the main federal law governing those plans. Before the department shares information or advice with an attorney for use in such a lawsuit, it would have to sign a written agreement describing that help and give a copy to any employer or plan official who could be harmed. The department would also have to report to Congress every year on these agreements, including logs of the information shared, conversations and meetings. The bill adds a statement to the law that it is national policy to encourage employers to voluntarily offer pension plans. As of February 20, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say a federal agency working behind the scenes with private lawyers suing employers should be open about it, and that discouraging employers from offering plans hurts workers' retirement security.
against: Critics say the notice and reporting rules would tip off employers under scrutiny and discourage the department from sharing information that helps workers recover lost retirement savings.
